layers.note: A columnar cactus to 12 m standing above the shrubs of the Arizona Upland, at most a few dozen a hectare, about one for every three foothill palo verdes on a bajada: placed in the open subcanopy, never a closed canopy.

moisture.note: Well-drained rocky slopes and upper bajadas; absent from wet ground.

heat_load.note: Most on warm south-facing slopes; at its cold limit only on them.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,200 m in the Sonoran Desert, thinning above.

shade_tolerance.note: Seedlings establish in a nurse plant's shade; adults stand in full sun.

coldest_c.note: Mild winters: coldest-month means from about 8 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Killed by freezes lasting into the day: lows to about −7 °C borne, gone below about −10 °C.

warmest_c.note: Hot summers: warmest-month means about 29 to 35 °C.

moisture_index.note: Arid: a moisture index from about 0.08 to 0.3.

summer_rain.note: Germinates only after the July and August monsoon, so it needs summer rain; it stops where summer rain ends at the Colorado River.

provenance.notes: Saguaro. A desert niche of plant forms F8's first placement (2026-10-07): authored from general knowledge of the species in the Sonoran Desert and checked against the Saguaro National Park places' CHELSA V2.1 climate (bajada 752 m, rocky hills 1,096 m), not yet against the public-domain FEIS reviews or fitted to occurrence records; the fit to GBIF occurrences over CHELSA comes with PlantGen (F8 in docs/roadmaps/PLANTS.md). Only the climate and site ranges niches have today: no soil, wash, spacing or nurse rules yet.
